checks.claim: Roman arch stones were held up during building on a temporary wooden frame called centering, removed once the keystone was set
checks.why: Centring is the temporary timber support of an arch, struck once the keystone makes the arch self-supporting.

checks.claim: An arch pushes outward on its supports, so its ends need heavy abutments to stop them spreading
checks.why: PBS Building Big: the abutments push back on the arch and keep its ends from spreading apart.

checks.claim: Some Roman bridges have small flood openings through their piers so floodwater can pass, as in the Pons Fabricius in Rome
checks.why: The small arch in the Pons Fabricius central pier lets high water flow through and takes pressure off the bridge.

checks.claim: Floods and scour, the riverbed washing away around piers, are the most common cause of bridge failure
checks.why: Studies put hydraulic causes (floods and scour together) first, about 53 percent of failures; scour alone is not separated in every study.

sources.title: ASCE study on causes of bridge failures 1989-2000
